name: Grade 3 — Science
subject: science
description: Water cycle, food chains, rocks, and plants

questions.question: Which part of a plant makes food using sunlight?
questions.explanation: Leaves contain chlorophyll which captures sunlight to make food through photosynthesis.

questions.question: What are clouds made of?
questions.explanation: Clouds are made of tiny water droplets or ice crystals floating in the sky.

questions.question: {{userName}} boils water and sees steam rising. This is an example of?
questions.explanation: When water is heated, it changes from liquid to gas (steam). This is called evaporation.

questions.question: In the water cycle, water vapor cools and forms clouds. This is called?
questions.explanation: Condensation is when water vapor cools and turns back into liquid water droplets, forming clouds.

questions.question: Rocks formed from cooled lava are called?
questions.explanation: Igneous rocks form when lava or magma cools and hardens. Examples: basalt, granite.

questions.question: Which organ pumps blood through the human body?
questions.explanation: The heart is a muscular organ that pumps blood through blood vessels to all parts of the body.

questions.question: A simple food chain is: grass → rabbit → fox. What is the grass called?
questions.explanation: Grass makes its own food using sunlight, so it is called a producer. Animals are consumers.

questions.question: {{userName}} leaves ice cubes on the table in summer. What happens to them?
questions.explanation: Ice (solid) melts into water (liquid) when temperature rises above 0°C. This is a change of state.

questions.question: What do we call the thin layer of air surrounding the Earth?
questions.explanation: The atmosphere is the layer of gases (mostly nitrogen and oxygen) that surrounds the Earth.

questions.question: How do bats navigate in the dark?
questions.explanation: Bats send out sound waves and listen to the echoes to detect objects — this is called echolocation.

questions.question: Animals that eat both plants and other animals are called?
questions.explanation: Omnivores eat both plants and animals. Examples: humans, bears, crows.

questions.question: What is the main source of energy for all life on Earth?
questions.explanation: The Sun provides light and heat energy. Plants capture solar energy through photosynthesis, starting all food chains.
